items.name: narration
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis, a short comic pause before each punchline ("some office commutes", "not 309", "left on its own"), a dramatic hush on "disappear", a playful snap on "Rewind.", and a slow, deadpan "The wrong sea."
lines: Narrator
You know the Danube: four capitals, ten countries. But you've never seen where part of it really goes.
Narrator
It starts in Germany's Black Forest, heading for the Black Sea.
Narrator
On the way: Vienna. Then, just 56 kilometres later... Bratislava.
Narrator
Two capitals, closer than some office commutes.
Narrator
Then it splits Budapest in half, and runs through Belgrade.
Narrator
Four capitals on one river. No river on Earth has more.
Narrator
So why, near its start, does it sometimes... disappear?
Narrator
Rewind. Near Immen-dingen, in Germany, the riverbed is limestone, full of cracks.
Narrator
The river leaks straight into the ground. In 1921, that stretch ran dry on 309 days.
Narrator
Rivers need days off too. Just... not 309.
Narrator
In 1877, scientists poured salt and dye into the cracks... and waited.
Narrator
60 hours later, it popped up 12 kilometres south, in a spring that flows into Lake Constance.
Narrator
Lake Constance drains into the Rhine. Which flows to the North Sea. The wrong sea.
Narrator
German states even took it to court, in 1927. Over water that left on its own.
Narrator
And the twist? Geologists think the upper Danube may one day switch to the Rhine... for good.
Narrator
Four capitals, ten countries... and a river that can't keep its own water.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
